question: Which thesis would make the better episode for this channel — more surprising, more useful to the viewer, and more defensible with data?

A.thesis: For many income-driven student loan borrowers, extra principal payments can destroy wealth because forgiveness tax risk is smaller than lost liquidity.
A.overturns: "Student loans should always be attacked before building real financial buffers."

B.thesis: Even with a big down payment, veterans' home loans have still priced below the best conventional tier, so their upfront fee has paid back within a few years.
B.overturns: "With a big down payment, a conventional loan beats paying the veteran loan fee."

A.thesis: Biweekly mortgage plans rarely beat a simple extra principal autopay, after enrollment fees, timing rules, and servicer posting delays are included.
A.overturns: "Biweekly mortgage payment programs are a secret hack for interest savings."

B.thesis: When mortgage rates actually fell, rising home prices historically ate only part of the payment relief, so the typical monthly payment still came down.
B.overturns: "If rates drop, home prices will jump and wipe out any savings."

A.thesis: A quick refinance after buying at a high mortgage rate is a coin flip: historically, large rate drops arrived within a few years less often than not.
A.overturns: "Marry the house, date the rate, you can always refinance later."

B.thesis: Choosing a longer auto loan often raises total car cost far beyond disclosed interest because it keeps borrowers underwater for longer.
B.overturns: "A longer auto loan is harmless if the monthly payment fits."

A.thesis: Living only on interest from safe short-term government bills left retirees exposed to sudden income collapses that lasted years, even though their principal never shrank.
A.overturns: "Never touching principal and living on interest alone gives retirees a stable, safe income."

B.thesis: A low cost target date fund left comparable savers with competitive after tax wealth in history, not a forecast, versus chasing recent winners.
B.overturns: "Managing your own funds should beat the boring default retirement option."

A.thesis: For borrowers with strong credit, a small down payment barely moves the locked mortgage rate, while a weaker credit score moves it several times as much.
A.overturns: "A bigger down payment is the surest way to get a lower mortgage rate."

B.thesis: A smaller down payment with mortgage insurance can outperform waiting to save more when rents rise and cash reserves prevent expensive debt.
B.overturns: "Avoid mortgage insurance at all costs before buying a home."

A.thesis: For low-bracket workers receiving refundable family credits, pretax retirement contributions can reduce future flexibility without meaningfully lowering today's tax bill.
A.overturns: "Pretax retirement saving is automatically the best tax move for every worker."

B.thesis: Indexing tax amounts to a slower inflation gauge costs a low-wage family with children a larger share of income than it costs a comfortable couple.
B.overturns: "Tax inflation adjustments fully protect every household from paying more as prices rise."

A.thesis: Capturing the workplace retirement match before sending extra cash to moderate interest debt often wins, even after tax and investment risk are modeled.
A.overturns: "Pay every debt down before investing for retirement at all."

B.thesis: Because each cost-of-living raise arrives months after prices rise, Social Security retirees lose purchasing power almost every year, adding up to many missing monthly checks over a retirement.
B.overturns: "Social Security's annual cost-of-living raise fully protects retirees' benefits from inflation."

A.thesis: Mortgage insurance on a small down payment could usually have ended years earlier through rising home values than through the legal paydown schedule, but only on request.
A.overturns: "You're stuck paying mortgage insurance until your balance falls far enough on schedule."

B.thesis: Buying mortgage points usually loses after typical homeowner turnover and refinancing chances are simulated, even when quoted break-even math looks comfortably positive.
B.overturns: "Paying points is smart whenever the rate break-even arrives before you move."

A.thesis: A nonrefundable vehicle credit can disappear for moderate-income buyers after family credits, making a cheaper used car win after taxes.
A.overturns: "A posted tax credit always lowers the car's real price."

B.thesis: Under current rules, an identical mortgage on an identical house can meaningfully cut federal income tax for a high-tax-state couple and do nothing for a low-tax-state couple.
B.overturns: "Paying mortgage interest gives every homeowner a tax break on their federal return."

A.thesis: Increasing paycheck withholding late in the year can prevent underpayment penalties more reliably than mailing catch-up estimated payments for gig income.
A.overturns: "Late estimated payments fix underpayment penalties as well as paycheck withholding."

B.thesis: College tuition credits use fixed income cutoffs, so a family that once qualified in full, with pay that merely kept pace with prices, now gets nothing.
B.overturns: "If our income only keeps pace with inflation, we keep qualifying for college tax credits."

A.thesis: At banks, stretching a new-car loan by an extra year has barely raised the interest rate, so nearly all the added cost comes from paying interest longer.
A.overturns: "Longer car loans cost more mainly because lenders charge a much higher rate."

B.thesis: With realistic dropout risk, the debt snowball can eliminate balances faster than avalanche math for borrowers juggling several credit cards.
B.overturns: "Always pay the highest interest card before any smaller balance."

A.thesis: Under the new child care rules, parents with modest wages usually keep more with the workplace child care account; the bigger credit wins only in a middle band.
A.overturns: "The bigger child care credit is the best deal for lower-income working parents."

B.thesis: For partners using marketplace health subsidies, marrying before year-end can raise combined tax owed versus staying unmarried until January, despite shared expenses.
B.overturns: "Marriage almost always creates a tax bonus for committed partners."

A.thesis: Maxing tax advantaged retirement accounts before using taxable brokerage usually improves long horizon outcomes, despite withdrawal rules and reduced flexibility.
A.overturns: "Taxable investing is almost as good because retirement accounts trap your money."

B.thesis: Whether required withdrawals from a retirement account grow or shrink after inflation depends on real interest rates, and at recent rates they keep rising until very old age.
B.overturns: "Required minimum withdrawals steadily drain a retirement account and shrink retirement income over time."

A.thesis: Prepaying a long mortgage on a short loan's schedule still costs more and takes longer than the short loan itself, because the lower short-term rate is forfeited.
A.overturns: "Take the long mortgage and pay extra; you get the same result with flexibility."

B.thesis: A higher-rate no-closing-cost refinance can leave borrowers richer than paying cash costs when remaining loan life is uncertain and payment savings are invested.
B.overturns: "Lowest mortgage rate is always the best refinance choice after fees."

A.thesis: Using a payroll-funded medical savings account often beats claiming medical deductions, because payroll taxes fall even when income deductions vanish.
A.overturns: "Medical expenses mainly help at tax time through itemized deductions."

B.thesis: In the lower brackets, the new break on car loan interest is worth less than a single point off the loan rate, and it shrinks for later loans.
B.overturns: "The new tax break makes borrowing for a new car dramatically cheaper."

A.thesis: Strategic conversions from pretax retirement accounts during low income retirement years can reduce lifetime taxes, even for households already in modest brackets.
A.overturns: "Conversions only help rich retirees facing very high future tax rates."

B.thesis: Rolling over short-term Treasury bills beat locking in a longer Treasury note held to maturity in a large share of past periods, especially when inflation was building.
B.overturns: "Locking in a longer-term bond rate always pays more than rolling over short-term cash."

A.thesis: Adding bonds during the final working stretch raised safe retirement income in bad historical sequences, history, not a forecast, even when average returns fell.
A.overturns: "Stocks always make the best retirement portfolio if your horizon feels long."

B.thesis: Holding government notes to maturity did not protect savers: notes bought in the later low-rate years all lost purchasing power by the time they repaid.
B.overturns: "If you hold a Treasury bond until it matures, you cannot lose money."

A.thesis: In every retirement-length stretch since the postwar years, a pension without cost-of-living raises lost a large share of its buying power, even during the calmest inflation periods.
A.overturns: "In a low-inflation era, a pension without cost-of-living raises holds its value well."

B.thesis: Delaying Social Security can beat claiming early and investing the checks for retirees near average health, because guaranteed inflation adjusted payments are hard to replicate.
B.overturns: "Claim early, invest the money, and markets will make waiting look foolish."

A.thesis: After inflation, the yearly cap on personal retirement account contributions is barely higher than when every worker first became eligible, and it covers fewer hours of typical pay.
A.overturns: "Retirement account contribution limits keep rising, so today's savers can shelter far more than earlier generations."

B.thesis: For long horizon savers, investing extra cash often beat prepaying low rate mortgages in history, not a forecast, even after taxes and volatility.
B.overturns: "The mortgage is guaranteed debt, so prepaying must beat retirement investing."

A.thesis: A single owner selling an ordinary median-priced home bought about a decade ago can now owe capital gains tax, because the tax-free limit never adjusts.
A.overturns: "Only owners of expensive homes ever pay tax when they sell their house."

B.thesis: Alternating charitable gifts into high-deduction filing periods can beat steady giving, even when total donations and cash flow stay unchanged.
B.overturns: "The tax benefit of giving depends only on total donated."
